svg.desc: Top view of the 141.35 by 141.35 inch BIOBUZZ field, audience at the bottom, red alliance on the left. Route self_shoot_only for the RED alliance, starting in tile C1, with 2 steps: 1 START at (57.9, 9.8, -90 deg); 2 SHOOT 4 at UP cell from (57.9, 9.8, -90 deg). First tip: we shoot the first tip. Estimated 5.5 s, POLLEN balance -4, up to 20 points for our robot; 0 errors and 1 warnings.

id self_shoot_only | start tile C1 | 2 steps | red ink | first tip: we shoot the first tip

g.title: Where a robot facing -90 degrees may be set up (rule G304): the tinted stretches of the own walls. The gaps are the FLOWERS, the LOADING ZONE, the corners and the center line.
g.text: tinted: where this start may stand (G304)

g.title: step 1: START at (57.9, 9.8, -90 deg) (t = 0.0 to 0.0 s) - Front edge ON the audience wall (the center of rotation is 9.77 in out), facing the wall, in line with the HIVE: a shooting pose, so the robot fires where it stands, with nothing to drive.

step 2: SHOOT 4 at UP cell from (57.9, 9.8, -90 deg) (t = 0.0 to 5.5 s) - The first tip. The UP cell holds 3 NECTAR, so the 3rd POLLEN tips the HIVE (+20) and the 4th is the spare for a field that needs one more. The camera stops the feeder only about 0.85 s after the tip, so the 4th is probably launched too and spent: that is the WARN on this step, and it is fine, it is only the spare. The robot fires from where it was put, with no drive first. Real teams land only about 6 shots in 10, so plan on this volley tipping the HIVE less than half of the time (the top-up routes are for that).

POLLEN: hold 4 at start, +0 taken, -4 fired, 0 at the end (balance -4) | Validator: 0 ERROR, 1 WARN

g.title: WARN step 2 [G417] step 2 (SHOOT): the HIVE tips with POLLEN 3 of the 4 (3 NECTAR in the cell; a cell tips at 8 POLLEN-equivalents (each POLLEN counts 1, each NECTAR 5/3)), but the camera cannot stop the feeder at once: the POLLEN that tips it is in the air for 0.50 s and the feeder stops about 0.85 s after it lands (Auto.TIP_STOP_LATENCY_SEC), while the next POLLEN leaves 1.00 s after the last. So the next 1 POLLEN will probably be launched into the cell while it swings down (G417: a launch at a rocking HIVE can spoil the tip; QA12 lets you add elements to a HIVE that is moving) and is spent: the plan counts 4 fired and 0 of the spare kept. The spare is for a field that needs one more POLLEN, not a POLLEN to carry on. Fire only 3 to keep it for sure (no spare then), or measure the real stop time on day one: with a latency under 0.50 s the spare stays in the robot
